hypotheses.justification: The other hypotheses already give it. The theorem takes `[IsPrincipalIdealRing O]` (with `[CommRing O]`), and Mathlib has the global instance `PrincipalIdealRing.isNoetherianRing [Semiring R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] : IsNoetherianRing R` (Mathlib/RingTheory/PrincipalIdealDomain.lean, line 115). If the variable is omitted, every place where `IPtHyp`, `ES`, `CSub`, `genericFibreES` and `β` need `IsNoetherianRing O` still finds it by instance synthesis. So the statement elaborates as written. `IsNoetherianRing` is a `Prop`-valued class, so proof irrelevance rules out any instance diamond. The proof (`rw [β, Equiv.trans_apply, AlgEquiv.arrowCongr_apply, liftSEquiv_apply]; rfl`) only unfolds `β` and `liftSEquiv`, does not depend on which instance term is used, and goes through unchanged. This is the case of a hypothesis implied by the others, like `[Nonempty α]` next to `[Inhabited α]`.
